method: Read the five modules' source (AI_PUZZLE, AI_PUZZLE_TRACK, AI_PUZZLE_TURN, AI_WHEEL_COLOURS/LAYOUT/AI_WHEEL, HEALTH_CHAT, the header of AI_RESULT_CHECKS) in 1.24.20 and 1.24.19, without the earlier reviews, the bench file or the changelog. Wrote every case by hand with its answer worked out first (rows left to right / queues front to back; walker x east y north; a die's tip away sends the top to the back; the painter's and the light colour wheels in hue order), most of them right inputs a person or a model would write, then ran each on both versions booted in Node + jsdom (the boot given in the brief). TRACK through Lantern.aiTrack.run; headless blocks through Lantern.aiPuzzle.find and run; wheels through Lantern.aiAct.build with the question, checking the plan's parts and the painted shapes (each part's inner wedge colour against the hue its name means, every ring and item sector for pink); bites through Lantern.healthNeed and Lantern.healthLessons (Bites = key health_bites); counts through Lantern.aiResultChecks.check(question, expr, Lantern.assist.run(expr), {parsed: Lantern.assist.parseReply(reply)}). A second pass of cases aimed at what 1.24.20 adds (capitalised names before places, bare left/right after another thing, 'add X and Y', the group words in the question, pronouns after 'bit'). Then random inputs for crashes and hangs: 6000 TRACK runs, 6000 puzzle texts, 6000 wheels, 8000 bite questions (both versions together), plus hand-made long lines. Verdicts: right; missed = a right input Lantern asks about (or, for wheels, leaves in groups where each colour should be a wedge; for bites, gives no Bites lesson); spoiled = a right input read or answered wrong (a wheel split that should have stayed, a Bites lesson for an animal); mended-wrong = an input that should go back (or prose) answered without a word; crash = an exception.
